roadmap.scope: Repo work only: move the indexer's search, 15-minute pass and probe onto a new Lambda composition root with the index as one S3 object, while the self-host openlore-indexer binary behaves exactly as before and stays AWS-free. Phases: walking skeleton, story lines, no-publish and write probe, error paths, probe, real adapter and runtime, infrastructure and CI, operator verbs. OUT OF SCOPE, stated plainly: anything that needs production action. No tofu apply, no lambda deploy, no trial, no cut-over, no DNS, no decommission. Those are operator stages after DELIVER; see operator_stages_after_deliver.

conventions.paradigm: ADR-007 functional Rust. decide (openlore-indexer-lambda), write_probe_outcome, location_names_write_probe_key and call_budget are pure. The pass, search and probe modes, the adapters and deploy.sh do I/O only. Plan-value rule (D-STZ-44): the pass work returns a value, and the no-publish arm holds the read port alone. Crafter: nw-functional-software-crafter.
conventions.tdd_phases: PREPARE, RED_ACCEPTANCE, RED_UNIT, GREEN, COMMIT (.nwave/des-config.json). RED_UNIT is recorded NOT_APPLICABLE with a reason on steps whose only RED is an acceptance scenario, a guard or a shell/tofu check.
conventions.test_paradigm: Acceptance suites already exist; DELIVER does not re-author them. Pure core: proptest in scale_to_zero_core.rs plus crafter-owned proptest with state-delta (tests/common/state_delta.rs) over a declared universe; single-example unit tests only with a `// bypass:` reason. In-process suites (layer 2), RIO, xtask and OP scenarios stay example-only: they verify wiring. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM for shell, tofu and workflow steps: the contract is a call log or a file's settings (DWD-STZ-28), compensated by the pure-core properties.
conventions.scenario_mapping: Every one of the 132 DISTILL scenarios appears in exactly one step's scenario_ids, RED driver first. scenario_fns are `<test target>::<fn>`. Targets: crate openlore-indexer-lambda: scale_to_zero_walking_skeleton, _search, _pass, _probe, _core. adapter-s3-index-object: scale_to_zero_object_store_real_io, scale_to_zero_write_probe. adapter-index-store: fingerprint_contract. xtask: scale_to_zero_architecture, scale_to_zero_platform. Steps with no DISTILL activation (01-02, 01-03, 06-04, 07-03, 07-04, 07-05, 08-10) name the test that guards them, which is shipped or crafter-owned, and leave scenario_ids empty. Non-scenario tests stay as they are: scale_to_zero_harness, the positive controls, the_stubs_answer_what_the_gates_will_ask, the_tofu_reader_reads_whole_values_in_the_right_block, the_secret_check_catches_each_shape_and_passes_a_plain_environment, the_seeds_really_reach_the_moto_store (activated with RIO in 06-03).
conventions.rider_classes: Each step names one RED driver (scenario_name). Other activations are a secondary driver (RED on activation, green within the step) or a guard (green on activation, or already active: record a mutation RED, revert it, and say so in the execution log). Un-ignore one scenario at a time.
conventions.rio_stay_ignored: EXCEPTION to 'DELIVER un-ignores'. RIO-1..9 and the seed check KEEP #[ignore]: rio-object-store runs `--run-ignored only` and demands all 10 by name, and un-ignoring RIO-1..8 would make the moto-less `test` job fail. DELIVER only edits their ignore reason to drop 'RED scaffold'. Activated means green against moto. Until 06-03 lands rio-object-store, RIO is enforced only locally, by the crafter's moto run in 06-01..06-03; CI does not run it. The job uses an explicit name filter, so a new ignored test cannot enter it silently.
conventions.test_edit_allow_list: (1) Remove the #[ignore] of a named scenario fn (RIO: reason text only). (2) One-line renames of var::* and Fault::token in tests/acceptance/support/indexer_lambda.rs (UI-5). (3) Stub output in scale_to_zero_platform.rs when deploy.sh reads a field with --query (its testability contract); order and refusal assertions stay. (4) Delete scale_to_zero_core.proptest-regressions if scaffold-panic seeds reappear before 01-05. (5) WS-1 and WS-2 drop their #[ignore], and its stale 'DELIVER step 1' reason, at activation (01-04, 01-10), and the suite header's 'first step' line names those steps. Forbidden otherwise: assertions, oracles, strategies, universe slots and test names. A scenario failing for a reason unrelated to its behaviour is a possible test bug (most have never run past init): stop and send it to nw-acceptance-designer. Crafter-owned tests may be added in their own crates and in xtask/tests/scale_to_zero_ci.rs.
conventions.green_before_commit: L-10: every test that is not #[ignore]d, the GUARD rows included, is green before any commit. Only #[ignore]d RED scenarios may be red. Stage by path, never commit -a. Commit locally; push only when the user says so.
conventions.test_runs: step_gate = `cargo build --bin openlore --bin openlore-indexer` (cli suites spawn the binary after 01-01), then for each touched crate `cargo nextest run -p <crate>`, plus `cargo test -p xtask`, `cargo xtask check-arch`, `cargo xtask check-probes`. Any step touching crates/openlore-indexer, adapter-xrpc-query-server, adapter-index-store or adapter-index-query also runs `cargo nextest run -p cli --test indexer_ingest --test appview_search --test indexer_deployment_walking_skeleton --test indexer_deployment_passes --test indexer_deployment_did_list --test indexer_deployment_public_surface --test indexer_deployment_core --test indexer_per_did_fetch --test indexer_per_did_resilience --test indexer_per_did_config --test indexer_pass_core`. Scoped crates only; CI verifies the workspace (host too slow).
conventions.self_host_unchanged: R-STZ-9 and P-1. The openlore-indexer binary's CLI, env vars, events, exit codes and hyper serve path do not change. A self-host behaviour change is a defect, in every step. Its proof: the shipped cli indexer suites, XS-2, and in CI serve-smoke and the artifact string check.
conventions.transitional_risks: All in-repo, nothing deployed. T1: 01-04..01-09 the pass publishes whenever it ran, with no start fetch, no fingerprint and the none-exists condition only, so only a first object works (WS-1 precedes FP and CORE in the handoff). It already stamps published-at, which WS-1 needs. PublishMetadata also requires pass_id, so 01-04 fills it, but no scenario pins it until PA-1. 01-10 closes T1: start fetch, publish on change, version condition. T2: until 03-02 the pass ignores its event; only `{}` reaches it; closed by CORE-7's caller. T3: until 02-05 search has no freshness gate. T4: until 06-04 main panics, so no image can run the root; nothing ships it until 07-03. T5: the write probe's refusal arrives in 03-01, though init calls the probe from 01-10.
conventions.decide_callers: CORE bodies land in 01-05 by handoff order; each gains its production caller in: publish_decision 01-10; dids_copy_usable 02-02; final_exit 02-03; freshness_due, reload_needed 02-05; pass_mode 03-02; not_live 05-01; served_index_stale 05-03. They are pub in the lib, so nothing is dead-code flagged meanwhile.
conventions.arch_rules_note: Each step's arch_rules names the xtask rules it adds or amends; each ships a synthetic violation unless a DISTILL XS scenario already plants one, and keeps `cargo xtask check-arch` green on the real tree. Criteria stay behavioural.
conventions.done_per_step: Scenario fns activated and green, guards recorded, arch_rules hold, the step's SCAFFOLD markers are gone, and every command in green passes.
conventions.mutation: Per-feature, kill rate >= 80% on modified files, after refactoring in each step. Scope (DEVOPS): decide.rs, pass_mode, served_index_stale, call_budget and each timeout, fingerprint, dispatch, the Lambda config parser, the S3 error mapping (404 vs other). Pure SDK call sites are excluded with the reason recorded.
conventions.wording: Event names, causes and fault tokens are pinned by the suites. PassFailure tokens (D-STZ-41) and IndexObjectWriteConditionIgnored already exist as vocabulary.

steps.name: Pure decisions: freshness, publish, liveness, exits, events, staleness
steps.description: All eight pure decisions in decide, as a batch: freshness_due, reload_needed, publish_decision, not_live, dids_copy_usable, final_exit, pass_mode, served_index_stale. No I/O: now and every outcome are arguments.
criteria: CORE-1, CORE-2, CORE-5: at most one check per TTL, a download only of a different index, and a DID copy usable up to 2 hours.
CORE-3: a pass publishes exactly when the index changed and stayed usable.
CORE-4, CORE-8: live only when every fact is good; stale only when it lags a record older than the margin.
CORE-6: the first failure wins; a pass that did not fail keeps its exit.
CORE-7: exactly two events are accepted and every other is refused.

steps.name: Index fingerprint: counts and a CID hash
